lines.text: Ilse said Measurers' lenses fog up whenever they come near me. Nobody knows why. So Tobin had an idea.
Steam lanterns, my lord! The rimeglass heats the water, the water makes fog. Put one in every doorway, and their fancy lenses will be as blind as a fish in milk.
...It works.
And when they ask why the whole village is full of smoke?
You tell them it's tradition.
What tradition?
You'll think of one.
As you all know, every midsummer, Greyhollow celebrates the ancient and sacred festival of smoke.
Since when?
Since this morning.
And us?
You and your hunters read like knights. You're going hunting in the Pale. For two weeks.
Two weeks in the Pale? Finally, some peace and quiet. No offence, my lord.
You're sending away your best fighters, right when the Order shows up.
I'm sending away my best evidence.
They left before dawn. Wren looked back once. I pretended not to see.
That left the hardest part. Teaching a hundred and twelve people how to be weak.
Right. A Measurer is watching you. You lift a sack of grain. Go.
No. No! You're a one-ring farmer. That sack is heavy. Drop it. Slower. Now groan.
Ugh?
Like you mean it.
Granny. Please. Miss the log. At least once.
I'm eighty-one, Sir Oswin. I don't miss.
The children were the worst. Children can't pretend to be anything. They just run, very fast, and laugh.
You realise this is the most ridiculous thing I have ever seen.
Yes. Is it working?
On a lens? Perhaps. On Hask?
Who's Hask?
My teacher. The finest Measurer in Aldmere. If he is one of those twelve, my lord, no amount of smoke will save us.
That night, every doorway in Greyhollow glowed with one of Tobin's lanterns, and the whole village sat inside its own small cloud.
And on the south road, twelve lights of a different kind came over the hill.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventeen, coming soon.
